title: No repository URL, code-availability or data-availability statement, in a paper that delegates its proofs to code
quote: Proofs are elementary and pinned by unit tests in the released code (76 tests;
explanation: 'Released' or 'committed' recurs in Sec. IV-B, V-C, V-F and VII, and Table IV is an entire table of test names offered as the evidence for six propositions whose proofs are not given in the body. Nine pages contain no URL, DOI, repository name, archive, or even an 'available upon publication' sentence. The verification chain is therefore unauditable by any reader, which is a reproducibility failure of a different order from a missing hyperparameter: the paper's argument for its own correctness is the artifact it does not provide. An availability statement naming the repository and the commit or tag that produced Table IV resolves it.

title: Every synthetic cell is a single seed with no dispersion, yet 0.035 margins carry the argument
quote: the net advantage concentrates exactly where pre-registered: distortion ($+0.035$), echo ($+0.035$), and label-free operation, which no grid can perform
explanation: results/tact_eval.json runs at config {items: 400, k: 15, k_max: 20, seed: 0}: one seed per cell, no repetitions, no interval on any accuracy. On 400 paired items a 0.035 difference is 14 items, and the paper's own paired counts elsewhere show discordance of that order arising in cells it treats as ties. Both pre-registered advantages, and the F4 verdict that rests on them, are single-draw quantities presented without sampling uncertainty. Repeating each adversarial cell over 10-20 seeds and reporting a mean with an interval, or giving the paired McNemar for each of the two +0.035 cells, would put the claim on the same footing as the grouped-cell result the paper already reports properly.

evidence_anchor.text: results/tact_eval.json config.seed = 0, single run per cell

title: The exponent cap differs between the two arms being compared, and the paper says the cap is what decides the comparison
quote: because its lower exponent cap ($2$ vs.\ $4$) regularizes better when $|D|\approx1$; cap robustness is left as an ablation
explanation: TACT-dev and TACT-LF are compared throughout as two variants of one method, but they are given different clips (4 vs 2) and different significance floors (1.28 vs 2.33). In the grouped cell the label-free arm wins, 0.940 vs 0.923, and the paper attributes the win to the cap rather than to the estimator. Since results/tact_eval.json shows gamma saturated at the cap in every headline cell, the cap is a free parameter that differs across arms and is deferred to future work precisely where it is decisive. Running both arms at both caps is a small run and would separate the estimator's contribution from the clip's.

title: Three of the five adversarial cells lie inside the estimator's invariance group by construction
quote: the adversarial regimes (distortions, heterogeneity, echo) lie outside the estimator's working model
explanation: The three monotone distortions are described in Sec. IV as 'rank-preserving by construction', and C1 establishes that TACT depends on confidence only through within-item ranks. A rank-invariant estimator facing rank-preserving distortions is being tested inside its own invariance group, not outside its working model: the result 1.000 in all three cells is entailed by the construction rather than discovered. This does not make the cells worthless, since they are exactly where the raw-value family fails and the comparison is the point, but they cannot also serve as the circularity mitigation the Discussion claims. Of the five, only the confident echo and the i.i.d. heterogeneity cell probe outside the working model.
